source_title: Entertainment Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn, Tiger Shroff’s Vimal Elaichi Ad Case To See Adjudication Next Week
source_excerpt:
The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has wrapped up the initial phase of its proceedings against Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn and Tiger Shroff, over their roles in promoting Vimal Elaichi. The cases now go before a senior officer for a formal decision, FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe told media at a press conference on Friday.
He added that all three actors had responded to the show-cause notices issued to them, while one of them, Ajay Devgn, had approached the Bombay High Court. Mundhe further stated that the cases had been referred to the Joint Commissioner, who is authorised to adjudicate the matter. He also indicated that the adjudication proceedings are likely to be taken up by next week.

“In response to the notices we issued, all three individuals responded and sought time. The Assistant Commissioner, who was the competent authority, has completed the proceedings and closed the hearings. The cases have now been referred to the Joint Commissioner, who is the competent authority for adjudication,” he said.

However, we are proceeding with the matter. We had initiated action and issued notices; all three individuals responded and sought time. The Assistant Commissioner, who was the competent authority, has completed the proceedings and closed the hearings. The cases have now been referred to the Joint Commissioner, who is the competent authority for adjudication. One of the individuals, Ajay Devgn, has approached the High Court."
Of the three, Ajay has taken the dispute to the Bombay High Court. “... One of the persons named, Ajay Devgn has approached the High Court,” he added.
Ajay’s petition describes the FDA’s show-cause notice as “arbitrary”, as he has maintained that he is no longer associated with the brand. A hearing in the matter has already taken place, and the court has listed it again for November 4.
Mundhe made clear that the legal challenge would not halt the regulator’s work. “We are proceeding with the matter,” he said, noting that Devgn was the only one of the named individuals to seek relief from the court.

For the unversed, Maharashtra FDA had issued show-cause notices to three actors in August, alleging that their advertisements for Vimal Elaichi amounted to surrogate promotion of the brand’s Pan Masala, a chewable product banned in Maharashtra. It had also sought the stopping of the promotional campaign and removal of related material from digital platforms.
